subsystems.name: Stimulus-responsive material
subsystems.role: changes shape or stiffness when its environment changes.

subsystems.name: Printed architecture
subsystems.role: encodes the intended movement in how the material is laid down.

subsystems.name: Trigger
subsystems.role: supplies the energy that drives the change.

subsystems.name: Multi-material printer
subsystems.role: builds stiff and soft phases in a single object, with time treated as a fourth design axis.

subsystems.name: Design and simulation tools
subsystems.role: predict, then invert, how a printed layout will deform.
parts: finite-element solver for swelling and thermal strain

subsystems.name: Sensing and control
subsystems.role: turns an actuated shape into a genuinely adaptive structure.

buildSteps.title: Define the transformation
buildSteps.detail: Decide the starting shape, the final shape, how many steps the change has, and which trigger is practical where the object will live.

buildSteps.title: Design and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Model the strain mismatch between stiff and soft regions so the printed object folds exactly as intended, or run inverse design to find a layout that produces a target shape.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the ink
buildSteps.detail: Mix a photopolymer or hydrogel with crosslinkers, and with fibres, nanoparticles or magnetic particles where extra stiffness or a non-thermal trigger is needed.

buildSteps.title: Print with programmed anisotropy
buildSteps.detail: Deposit material so fibres, layers and material boundaries run in chosen directions; the mismatch between them is what makes the flat sheet fold later.

buildSteps.title: Fix the temporary shape
buildSteps.detail: For shape-memory polymers, heat above the transition temperature, deform the object, then cool it under load so it holds the programmed shape until triggered again.

buildSteps.title: Cure and post-process
buildSteps.detail: Fully cure the resin, remove supports, and hydrate hydrogels so they reach their working state.

buildSteps.title: Trigger and characterise
buildSteps.detail: Apply heat, moisture, light or a field and measure how fully, how fast and how repeatably the object returns to its target shape.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and instrument
buildSteps.detail: Embed the printed element in a larger assembly and add sensors and control where the structure must respond to real conditions rather than a lab trigger.

prerequisites.why: the movement comes from joining materials with different responses, which needs printers that can place several materials in one build.
these provide the reversible shape change itself; most are still laboratory formulations.
without accurate prediction, designers must iterate physically instead of engineering a shape deliberately.

prerequisites.tech: Cyclic durability of soft active materials
prerequisites.why: building components are expected to actuate thousands of times over decades; most printed actuators have been tested for far fewer cycles.
an adaptive structure must know its own state, otherwise it is merely a passively deforming object.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of self-folding sheets and printed actuators
pathway.unlocks: a catalogue of materials, print recipes and deformation models.

pathway.milestone: deployable devices such as medical implants, self-deploying space hardware and soft grippers
pathway.unlocks: commercial experience with printed parts that must actuate reliably in service.

pathway.milestone: building-scale components that respond passively to sun, heat or humidity — shade elements, vents and seals
pathway.unlocks: adaptive behaviour with no motors or power supply.

pathway.milestone: instrumented smart structures combining printed actuators with sensing and control
pathway.unlocks: buildings and infrastructure that adjust shape or stiffness in response to load and weather.
